items.title: NVIDIA Flare v0.4.0 adds pure-CUDA lossless KV-cache compression and parallel Engram gathers
items.summary: NVIDIA's hyperflare-inference (Flare) v0.4.0 compresses prefix-cache checkpoints losslessly on the GPU at the VRAM to DRAM boundary, with a matching Rust CPU decoder, so revisited long sessions restore instead of recomputing. A tester on two DGX Sparks reports a Qwen 3.8 Flash Next continuation wait falling from 229.8 s to 170.6 s, and the release also parallelizes Engram table gathers (128K DeepSeek V4.1 Flash GPU wait 3,769 ms to 21.3 ms in their notes).

doubt.pushback: The 3.9x revisit figure is the PR's own run and the DGX Spark timing is one tester's single workload; no independent repro yet.

items.title: DHH's blind overnight Omarchy eval: Inkling 2 Mini scores 8.50 vs Qwen3.8 27B 8.00 on a 48-64 GB RTX Spark
items.summary: DHH gave three local models the same Omarchy jobs overnight (a theme, a plugin, an app and a game), judged blind out of 10: Inkling 2 Mini scored 8.50 and finished all 8 runs in 142 minutes, Qwen3.8 27B 8.00 with 7 of 8 in 240 minutes, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 4.38. Omarchy has added Inkling 2 Mini to its local model catalog and published a reproducible measurement: 32.7 GB loaded and about 78 to 92 tok/s decode on a 64 GB NVIDIA N1X laptop via TensorFold.

doubt.pushback: Eval prompts and judge rubric are not published; one quoter notes judge calibration across 8 runs could move averages by more than half a point.

reception.summary: Repliers and quoters mostly agree Inkling 2 Mini is best in class for the 48-64 GB tier; AkitaOnRails ran his own small benchmark and found it level with or slightly ahead of Qwen 3.8 27B, others report using it as a daily local agent; asks for published prompts, power and tok/s numbers, and long tool-loop tests.
